nodes.description:
Reads one track at a MoQ relay into the graph — how a stream reads another stream's exposed port, on this machine through the local relay's loopback listener or on another machine through any relay that serves it, and how it reads a track any other MoQ publisher wrote. The track is named by `broadcast` and `track`, each exactly as its publisher wrote it: a stream's exposed port is the track `<node>/<port>` of the broadcast `<machine>/<stream id>.hang`.

`track` carries each object's payload bytes as the relay delivered them, the first object of each group starting a group, and its catalog entry is the track's own from the broadcast's catalog. What a payload means is the publisher's: a `VideoFrame` track names surfaces on the machine that wrote it, which mean nothing here.

Groups reach `track` in sequence order, whatever order the relay delivers them in. A missing group is waited for until newer content on the track runs `max_age` milliseconds past it, measured in the track's own timestamps and never on a clock, until its stream is reset, or until the track ends; then it is given up and the next group read. The read joins at the live edge.

The relay's object carries the writer's stamp, on the writer's clock. Every stamp in a graph is this machine's, so `track` is stamped with the object's own timestamp — the hang container's for a media track, the object's otherwise — plus one offset taken at the first object and lowered for an object that would run more than 100 ms ahead of its arrival, as the stack's own player lowers its reference past its buffer, such as the group in progress a joining reader is handed in one burst; it is taken again when the track steps back or falls a second behind, so the track's own spacing survives jittered arrival. An object carrying no timestamp is stamped at arrival.

A relay that refuses, or a track not yet published or withdrawn, is retried with backoff and never ends the stream.

broadcast.description: The broadcast's path at the relay, exactly as its publisher wrote it. A stream's is `<machine>/<stream id>.hang`.

max_age.description: How far newer content on the track may run past a missing group, in whole milliseconds of the track's own timestamps, before the group is given up; the history asked of the relay, clamped to what the track keeps. A transport budget, never a playout delay.

relay_url.description: The relay to subscribe at. The default is this machine's local relay on loopback, which serves every private and public port of the machine.

track.description: The track of `broadcast` to read, exactly as its publisher named it. An exposed port's is `<node>/<port>`.

outputs.name: track
outputs.description: Each object of the track, as the relay delivered it
